notes: Dubai's official registry (Dubai Pulse / DLD) is not yet connected for this market; access is pending approval. DLD data below is as shown on property portals, graded by how many independent sites agree.

findings.claim: Creek Bay Tower B and Creek Haven Tower B are new residential towers in Dubai Creek Harbour, with one-bedroom apartments from AED 1.9 million.
Dubai Creek Harbour apartments generally transact around AED 2,600 per sq ft, roughly 14% below comparable Downtown Dubai pricing, per DLD data cited via Property Monitor.

An independent Dubai listings aggregator tracking 17 Emaar projects in Dubai Creek Harbour reports that 3 of the 17 are past the handover date their developer published, with units still listed for sale.
The wider Dubai Creek Harbour master plan spans roughly 6 square kilometres and is being developed by Emaar Properties in partnership with Dubai Holding.
A property marketing site states that Emaar has never cancelled a project in Dubai and that no buyer has ever lost a deposit.
Dubai Land Department data shown on property portals lists Creek Bay as an active registered project of Dubai Creek Harbour L.L.C., with handover in April 2030.
One portal quoting DLD registry data gives Creek Bay's project number as 4198 and records it as escrow protected.

Emaar has completed and handed over homes in Dubai Creek Harbour: it reported thousands of handovers there and across Dubai, and a DLD-based tracker records its Creek Beach Canopy/Moor as completed in November 2025.
Emaar Development reported record property sales of AED 71.1 billion for 2025.
The master plan's central Creek Tower remains paused.

On Trustpilot, Emaar has about 117 reviews averaging 1.5 out of 5; several owners, including in Creek Beach and Dubai Creek Harbour, complain of construction quality and after-sales service. Trustpilot notes Emaar does not invite reviews, so they may not be representative.

reading.observation: One marketing site states Emaar has never cancelled a project and no buyer has ever lost a deposit. An independent listings aggregator reports that 3 of Emaar's 17 tracked Creek Harbour projects are past their own published handover date, with units still listed. A missed handover date is not a cancellation or a lost deposit, but the absolute claim rests on a single promotional source, and nothing checked here verifies it.

questions.question: Please show me this tower's DLD project registration number and its entry on the Dubai REST app or Dubai Pulse.
questions.good: A specific project number that can be looked up independently.
questions.red_flag: ‘It's registered, don't worry’ with no number given.

questions.question: Has Emaar missed a published handover date on any comparable Dubai Creek Harbour tower, and if so, what happened to buyers' payments?
questions.good: A specific, named example with a factual outcome.
questions.red_flag: A flat denial with no specific example addressed.

questions.question: Which escrow account is this payment going into, and can I get RERA's own escrow account confirmation for this specific project?
questions.good: A named escrow account with RERA confirmation.
questions.red_flag: Any account not confirmed as the project's registered escrow account.

questions.question: Can an independent snagging inspection be done before handover, and how long does Emaar commit to fixing what it finds?
questions.good: A written snagging process with repair timelines.
questions.red_flag: “Any issues can be raised after you move in.”
